key_insight: Clinical QA skill does not reliably translate into correct treatment changes when patient context shifts, and pivot-sensitive training helps models adapt better.
clinical_relevance: For AI tools used in care planning, models must be tested on decision changes under new constraints, not just on factual medical questions.
method: Built ClinPivot, an auditable benchmark for treatment decisions using biomedical relations and pivoted patient contexts.
Compared frontier medical QA models and task-adapted Qwen variants on whether they change treatment choices appropriately.
Evaluated decision-structured supervision and lightweight replay for improving pivot-sensitive decision-making and assistant ability.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that strong medical QA performance did not reliably predict treatment-decision performance, and model rankings changed across evaluation regimes.
watch_item: ClinPivot appears focused on benchmarked decision shifts, so real-world clinical deployment would still need validation across broader patient scenarios and safety constraints.
paper_title: Do Clinical Models Change Treatment Decisions?
